I now have the full picture. MemoService is served over two HTTP-based protocols, not native gRPC (there's no `RegisterMemoServiceServer` gRPC-server call — that was a certified zero). The two protocols are gRPC-Gateway (REST/JSON transcoding) and Connect.

q19.

**gRPC-Gateway (REST/JSON transcoding) — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:108`**
`v1pb.RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s)` registers MemoService onto the grpc-gateway mux, mounted under `/api/v1/*` (v1.go:128). The generated handler it depends on lives in `proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.gw.go`.

**Connect — `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go:40`**
`wrap(apiv1connect.NewMemoServiceHandler(s, opts...))` builds the Connect handler; it's mounted via `RegisterConnectHandlers` under the `/memos.api.v1.*` route group (v1.go:141, 144). The generated `NewMemoServiceHandler` it wraps is in `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/memo_service.connect.go:461`.

Both protocols reuse the same `*APIV1Service` implementation — the file comment at `connect_handler.go:17-20` states this design explicitly ("Support both native gRPC and Connect protocols… single source of truth for business logic"). Note that despite that comment's wording, MemoService is not actually registered on a native gRPC server anywhere in `server/` — `RegisterMemoServiceServer` has zero callers (certified by the map). The two live registrations are the gRPC-Gateway and Connect ones above.
